overall: I'm Wei. I live ten minutes from my parents, weekly hotpot is non-negotiable, and my spouse and I pull on banners on the couch. This run mostly gets me. The best cards know that family duty is love and resentment in the same breath: the 'optional' Sunday dinner, 'Relief that I'm not an only child', the Grumbler and the Secret sponsor. Where the family chapter misses, it treats duty as logistics and not as a negotiation. Real families don't decide care with a shared calendar. The parent says they're fine, the far sibling pays while the near one shows up, someone suggests a caregiver and dinner goes silent, the grandparents are the daycare plan, and plans get changed by sending an auntie in first. Build those moves into C6-4, C6-2, C3-9 and C6-7. There's also a card missing for anyone married: "The big holiday. Both families want you at dinner, same night." / Two dinners. Eat twice, smile twice. / Alternate years, set in stone. / Host both families at ours. Chaos, one table. / Whoever's parents asked first. (teen costume: both sets of grandparents). And nothing asks about money going up to parents, which for a lot of us is the biggest family line item. One scoring worry: R1 reads family deference as wanting closeness. Keeping the peace at home is not the same pull as wanting your person close, and diaspora players will land on 'We' for reasons that are really duty. Keep circumstance options on the family cards and score peace-keeping lighter. Structure: 76 cards against a 56 to 64 target, and 14 sealed cards where the brief says 8 in the finale. That's the fatigue that killed test 1. Visible repeats Jerry will catch by card 8: three bill-split cards (C3-3, C4-9, C4-11), two head-start hot takes (C4-2, C5-3), 'already has a job/plans' three times, 'before they finish the sentence' twice, 'Fair is fair' twice, instant noodles twice. Cut C4-11 and C5-3 and fix the lines. In chapter 6 the two this_or_that cards stand alone instead of a round of 3, and C6-9 then C6-S1 are both R3 back to back. Last, a small cultural catch: hotpot is the classic holiday meal in many Chinese homes, so it can't be the 'something totally different' answer.
